newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing. [CORRECTED 15:16 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing. [CORRECTED 15:16 GMT]

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Monday:

Spokesman Peter Guilford briefed on tomorrow's EU/U.S. meeting in Washington which will prepare EU/U.S. summit at the end of May. He said the EU delegation would include Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan and Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo (Corrects Commissioner from Karel Van Miert) and would start with a pre-breakfast meeting at 0730/1230 GMT.

The EU delegation will meet U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, the Commerce Department's undersecretary for international trade Stuart Eizenstat, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky, Guilford said.
Asked to react to a report in Belgian newspaper Le Soir on genetically modified maize, spokesman Peter Jorgensen said it was not new that some people did not agree with the Commission's decisions.
Jorgensen also said it had been decided to make the conclusions of the scientific committees on Food, on Animal Nutrition and on Pesticides available and that a copy would be available in his office.
In answer to a question, spokeswoman Barbara Nolan confirmed that Britain had opposed the creation of a European observatory on racism and xenophobia, therefore blocking the project.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/57: The Commission is convening a conference in Brussels on 6 and 7 February for transit operators and authorities from 31 European countries - Euro Transit 97.
- Speech/97/19: Opening speech by Commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard to the hearing on the IGC and the environment.
- Speech/97/20: Speech by Commissioner Wulf-Mathies on "Social and economic cohesion in Europe: implication for Britain".
- Speech/97/21: Speech by Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan to the CEEC anti-dumping seminar.
- Eurostat news release No 6/97: EU 2.9 bn ECU in the red with NAFTA.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - External trade No 1996-12: European Union trade with NAFTA - Results until 1995.
